reuse.why: Fintegra linking reuses linkSimpleFinAccount via a syncSource parameter and the guards are shared, but the new downloadTokenTransactions is not adopted by Akahu and the detach reset re-types unlinkAccount's field block.

duplication.why: Six identical one-line per-provider assert wrappers, six registration lambdas repeating the same two guard calls, downloadTokenTransactions duplicating downloadAkahuTransactions (which stays), and a copy of unlinkAccount's reset.

placement.why: The guards are wired into the app.method registration lambdas instead of the link handlers themselves, so the rules live in RPC wiring and AccountHandlers' typeof link* no longer describe the enforced behaviour.

scope.why: Focused on the four requested behaviours plus tests and the SYNC_PROVIDERS entry; reordering the syncAccount if-chain is minor churn.

maintainability.why: Speculative per-provider wrapper layer, a half-generalised token download with a hard-coded provider ternary, an assert that mutates, and a SimpleFin handler stretched with an 'orgDomain' in-check to also serve Fintegra make this awkward to own.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No existing abstraction is circumvented; the new guards are routed through by all six link registrations (the detach reset copies unlinkAccount, which carries provider cleanup, so it is duplication rather than bypass).

disguised_duplication.where: sync.ts downloadTokenTransactions is a reshaped, provider-parameterised copy of downloadAkahuTransactions while Akahu keeps its own copy; the six assert*AccountAvailable wrappers dress the same call up under different names.

abstraction_drift.where: linkSimpleFinAccount gains syncSource plus an 'orgDomain' in externalAccount branch to serve Fintegra; assertBankAccountIsNotLinked gains replaceExistingLink; downloadTokenTransactions has a fintegra/akahu ternary yet syncAccount still calls downloadAkahuTransactions directly.
